subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should stored `/exec` session defaults be allowed to override later global or per-agent exec security policy, or should operator config bound/reset those stored values?
rationale: Current code, docs, and tests treat `/exec` as durable per-session state, but the issue shows that durability can weaken later operator security changes; automation cannot choose that security/compatibility boundary safely.

options.title: Make operator config authoritative
options.body: Global and per-agent exec policy would bound or reset persisted session exec fields, with migration or doctor handling for existing sessions.

options.title: Keep durable `/exec` precedence
options.body: Current session-default behavior remains documented, and operators must clear or rotate sessions when changing exec security policy.

options.title: Add explicit reset first
options.body: Maintain existing precedence for now but add an operator-facing reset or doctor repair path before changing default behavior.

recommendation.title: Make operator config authoritative
recommendation.body: Global and per-agent exec policy would bound or reset persisted session exec fields, with migration or doctor handling for existing sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the current `/exec` session contract is the original session-override implementation and follow-up test ownership.
